concerns.concern: The rise in cycle-to-cycle correlation may simply mean the device never fully returns to the insulating Off state during the ~3 s off period, or that accumulated Joule heating raises the baseline temperature. No Off-state diffraction or per-cycle electrical data are shown to rule this out.
concerns.quote: Successive On-state images would then become correlated because the system stops fully switching, not because it "learned".

concerns.concern: The small changes in correlation could come from instrumental or extrinsic effects rather than domain rearrangement. These include sample or stage drift, Bragg-peak shifts from thermal expansion or strain, and changes in total diffracted intensity. None of these is excluded.
concerns.quote: Decorrelation or recorrelation can arise from several sources unrelated to domain rearrangement

concerns.concern: Hours of intense X-ray exposure can by itself cause persistent metallization and defects in VO₂. Dose-dependence, fresh-spot or beam-blanked controls are needed to separate X-ray-driven from current-driven changes.
concerns.quote: X-ray exposure is known to induce persistent metallization and defect formation in VO₂, and the dose here is about 2×10¹⁰ ph/s for hours.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature 'experimental stability limit' is internally inconsistent. The 4 mA On-state relaxation time is longer than that limit despite higher temperature and Joule heating, so either the baseline is not a true limit or the On-state τ is not meaningful.
concerns.quote: Either the baseline is not the limit, or the On-state τ is not meaningful.

concerns.concern: The stretching exponent β, on which the jamming claim rests, is probably not determinable. The decay is observed only to about 10% of τ, where τ and β are strongly covariant and β depends on subtle curvature in noisy data.
concerns.quote: In this regime τ and β are strongly covariant, and β is set by subtle curvature in the noisiest part of the data.

concerns.concern: A single global τ is imposed for all aging times while β is left free. Any real aging of τ is therefore artificially converted into an apparent drift of β.
concerns.quote: Any true aging of τ will therefore be absorbed into an apparent drift of β.

concerns.concern: 'Deterministic switching' is asserted without measuring any electrical switching statistics versus cycle number, such as threshold, delay-time distributions or voltage variance.
concerns.quote: No electrical statistics versus cycle number are presented.

concerns.concern: The claim that sub-threshold current erases memory and restores stochastic switching is untested. The only sub-threshold experiment starts from the as-prepared state, and no train → erase → retrain sequence or retention test is shown.
concerns.quote: No train → erase → retrain sequence is shown.

concerns.concern: β was never extracted from the cycling experiment, so the link between jamming and switching stochasticity in the title is inferred rather than measured.
concerns.quote: The connection between jamming and stochasticity ("Jamming-controlled stochasticity") is inferred, not measured.

concerns.concern: The jamming times at 0.26 and 1.7 mA are indistinguishable, and the 4 mA curve does not saturate. The claimed trend of slower transitions at larger current, and the shear-thickening analogy, are therefore unsupported.
concerns.quote: The claimed trend "larger current, slower transition" and the shear-thickening analogy are therefore unsupported.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold 0.26 mA dataset also shows the 'jamming transition'. This contradicts the claim that electrical switching is what induces jamming.
concerns.quote: This contradicts the statement that "electrical switching induces a jamming transition".

concerns.concern: A compressed exponential (β > 1) is not specifically evidence of jamming. The authors need to discuss alternatives such as stress- or strain-relaxation-driven ballistic motion known from soft matter.
concerns.quote: discuss why β > 1, a compressed exponential, should be read as jamming rather than, for example, stress- or strain-relaxation-driven ballistic motion

concerns.concern: Speckle correlation of the whole illuminated area is not equivalent to deterministic filament formation. Most of the illuminated VO₂ lies outside the filament, so the signal mixes filament and matrix contributions.
concerns.quote: A rise in speckle correlation of the whole illuminated area is not equivalent to deterministic filament formation.

concerns.concern: The correlation function in Eq. 1 is not the standard normalized form and is sensitive to total intensity changes, for example from M1/R phase-fraction changes. The 'immediate erasure' at 4 mA may partly reflect intensity or peak-position changes.
concerns.quote: As written, it is sensitive to changes in total intensity, which occur when the M1/R phase fraction changes on switching or heating.

concerns.concern: The X-ray footprint is substantially larger than the 5×5 µm² channel. The speckle therefore includes VO₂ outside the current path and possibly near electrodes that heat and expand, and the current-carrying fraction is not given.
concerns.quote: the footprint along the beam is enlarged by roughly 1/sin θ, so it is substantially larger than the 5 × 5 µm² channel.

concerns.concern: The Joule-heating interpretation is inconsistent. Under 4 mA current the relaxation time is longer than at room temperature, contrary to the Arrhenius prediction for a heated system.
concerns.quote: Yet τ under 4 mA (1.6×10⁵ s) is longer than at 298 K (8.1×10⁴ s)

concerns.concern: All current-dependent data come from one device, apparently measured sequentially. Because the paper claims the device retains memory, the order of experiments and any reset protocol between runs must be stated.
concerns.quote: the order of experiments and any reset protocol (e.g. thermal cycling above T_c) between the 0.26 mA, 1.7 mA, 4 mA and cycling runs must be stated.

concerns.concern: No repeat runs show that the ~200-cycle onset and ~1000-cycle saturation of correlation are reproducible.
concerns.quote: Repeat runs are needed to show that the ~200-cycle onset and ~1000-cycle saturation are reproducible.

concerns.concern: The normalization of the cycle-to-cycle correlation ΔG(n, n+1) plotted from 0 to 1 is undefined. Raw values, the static-configuration expectation and the shot-noise floor are not given.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3i spans 0 to 1 "normalized correlation", but the normalization (min–max? relative to static frames?) is not given.

concerns.concern: Without the full G(n, n+k) dependence on k after training, convergence to a fixed configuration cannot be distinguished from slow drift.
concerns.quote: The full G(n, n+k) dependence on k after training would distinguish convergence to a fixed configuration (deterministic) from slow drift.

concerns.concern: The Arrhenius activation energy is effectively a two-point slope. One point is the instrument limit and the other lies in the non-stationary middle of the metal-insulator transition.
concerns.quote: This is consistent with the quoted 2700 ± 800 K but shows the "fit" is a two-point slope.

concerns.concern: Comparing the activation energy (in kelvin) to the VO₂ melting temperature has no clear physical basis. It should instead be compared with relevant barriers such as domain-wall pinning, nucleation or oxygen-vacancy migration.
concerns.quote: Comparing an activation energy expressed in kelvin to the VO₂ melting temperature has no clear physical basis.

concerns.concern: No estimate of the local temperature rise from Joule heating is given, for example from Bragg-peak shifts or a thermal model.
concerns.quote: No estimate of the local temperature rise is given; the power at 0.26 mA is about 0.5 mW, at 4 mA about 8 mW.

concerns.concern: The ~1000 s delay before decorrelation under sub-threshold current is comparable to sample-holder thermal equilibration times. It should be compared with a control in which the stage temperature is stepped by an equivalent amount.
concerns.quote: is comparable to typical thermal equilibration times of a sample holder after a step in dissipated power.

concerns.concern: The pristine (non-irradiated) device control is only in an unavailable Supplement. The role of Ga irradiation in the learning effect should be shown in the main text.
concerns.quote: The pristine-device data are referred to the Supplemental Information, which is not available.

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether the M1 and R Bragg peaks are resolved on the detector, which region of interest is analysed, and whether the peaks are analysed separately.
concerns.quote: It is not stated whether these are resolved on the detector, which ROI is analysed, or whether they are analysed separately.

concerns.concern: The main text and Methods give conflicting descriptions of the Ga⁺-irradiated region: a central 5×5 µm region versus global irradiation.
concerns.quote: The main text states that a central 5 × 5 µm region was irradiated with Ga⁺. The Methods state that devices were "globally irradiated".

concerns.concern: The 1.7 mA dataset appears only in Fig. 4. Its position relative to the characteristic currents, whether a filament forms, and its two-time plot are not provided.
concerns.quote: The 1.7 mA dataset appears only in Fig. 4. Its position relative to I_on, I₁ and I₂ in Fig. 5b

concerns.concern: Several numbers disagree between text and figures: the room-temperature limit, the On-state τ and the sub-threshold current. The τ in Fig. 3g is also not discussed in the text.
concerns.quote: room-temperature limit: 8000 ± 3000 s (text) vs 81000 ± 3000 s (Fig. 2c)

concerns.concern: The text refers to a nonexistent inset in Fig. 3i. It also describes the correlation stabilization inconsistently ('for' versus 'after' ~1000 cycles).
concerns.quote: The text refers to "the inset (orange data)" in Fig. 3i, but there is no inset

concerns.concern: The Methods notation is wrong in two places. The t_age definition for the lines is inconsistent, and Eq. 3 is mislabeled as a single exponential when it is stretched or compressed.
concerns.quote: Eq. 3 is called a "single exponential" but is a stretched or compressed exponential.

concerns.concern: The cycling timing is ambiguous. On time, off time and frame position within the pulse need to be specified and checked against the cycle-number axis.
concerns.quote: "Turned on and off for 3 s" could mean 3 s on and 3 s off, or a 3 s period.

concerns.concern: The domain-size estimate needs the direction of the peak width. Instrumental resolution, finite-thickness broadening and microstrain should also be separated.
concerns.quote: The domain size R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM = 20 nm needs the direction of Q_FWHM.

concerns.concern: The measured speckle contrast should be compared with the value expected from the coherence length, beam size and pixel size, to show the data are speckle-limited rather than background-limited.
concerns.quote: Speckle contrast (≈2–3%) should be compared with the value expected from the 1.7 µm coherence length, beam size and pixel size

concerns.concern: Fig. 5b lacks definitions of I_on, I_off, I₁ and I₂. The 313 K resistance and On/Off ratio are not given, which matters because the irradiated device's resistance ratio is modest.
concerns.quote: Fig. 5b: please define I_on, I_off, I₁ and I₂ in the caption.

concerns.concern: Analogies to granular jamming and shear-thickening go beyond the evidence. They should be softened or backed by a quantitative model such as a percolation or packing threshold.
concerns.quote: are analogies that go beyond the evidence. Either soften them or support them with a quantitative model

concerns.concern: Figs. 2a and 2b use different color scales, which hinders visual comparison.
concerns.quote: Figs. 2a and 2b use different color scales (1.01–1.02 vs 1.01–1.03), which hinders visual comparison.
